title: Infecting kidney organoids with a cDNA reporter clone of SARS-CoV-2
protocol: Seed Vero E6 cells in a clearly labeled T-175 flask(s) at a seeding cell density of 18 × 10^6 cells per flask (85%–90% confluency) in 25 mL complete DMEM.
Incubate flasks overnight in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Determine cell number using the additional flask prepared as follows: aspirate medium from flask and wash once with 12 mL PBS.
Add 5 mL 0.05% trypsin-EDTA and incubate flask in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Monitor for cellular detachment using an inverted phase-contrast microscope. Gentle tapping of the flask is encouraged.
Detachment should take no longer than 5 min.
Add 3 mL complete DMEM to the flask to inactivate trypsin.
Gently wash the cell monolayer several times using a serological pipette to create a single-cell suspension.
Collect the cell suspension into a 50 mL conical tube.
Wash the flask twice with 8 mL complete DMEM to collect residual cells.
Transfer the washes into the same 50 mL conical tube used for collecting the original cell suspension.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 500 × g for 10 min.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 8 ml complete DMEM.
Perform a cell count per flask using any desired method, such as a hemocytometer.
Calculate the required volume of stock icSARS-CoV-2-mNG to achieve an MOI of 0.01 based on the total cell number per flask.
Prepare viral inoculum to a final volume of 2.5 ml per flask in serum-free DMEM.
Remove a stock virus-containing vial from -80°C storage.
Thaw the virus in a 37°C water bath (2-5 min).
Transfer the tube to BSC and mix by pulse-vortexing for 10 s within the BSC.
Retrieve the T-175 flask(s) of Vero E6 cells from the 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Remove medium from the flask(s).
Add 2.5 mL viral inoculum to each flask directly.
Seal the flask cap using parafilm.
Rock the flask(s) gently by hand to distribute virus inoculum over cells.
Transfer the sealed flask(s) to a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator for 1 h.
Gently rock the flask back-and-forth by hand once every 10 min during the first hour.
Add 17.5 mL low-serum DMEM directly to viral inoculated flask(s).
Transfer the sealed flask(s) to a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator and incubate for 40–48 h.
Monitor for cytopathic effects (CPE) using an inverted phase-contrast microscope after 40 h post infection.
Monitor for viral gene expression by detection of green fluorescence produced in infected cells.
Infect Vero E6 cells with icSARS-CoV-2-mNG at a MOI of 0.01 for 1 hour with intermittent shaking.
Monitor cytopathic effects (CPE) at 26 and 45 hours post-infection for Stock 1.
Monitor cytopathic effects (CPE) at 41 hours post-infection for Stock 2 using an inverted phase-contrast microscope with or without exposure to GFP LED.
Harvest when cytopathic effects are visible and remaining adherent cells fluoresce green.
Transfer infected flasks to a biological safety cabinet (BSC).
Transfer virus-containing supernatant to 50 mL conical tubes.
Distribute equal volumes of virus-containing medium into each tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 500 × g for 10 minutes to clear cellular debris.
Filter the cleared virus-containing supernatant using a 0.45 μm filter into a new 50 mL conical tube.
Mix supernatant thoroughly by pulse-vortexing for 10 seconds.
Transfer the resulting centrifuged supernatant into a new tube.
Mix well by repeated inversion or pipetting if a vortex is not available within the BSC.
Aliquot resulting viral supernatant into externally threaded cryogenic tubes for single-use workable stocks.
Use 0.25 mL per tube which produces approximately 80 tubes per T-175 flask.
Place the aliquots at -80°C for long-term storage.
Seed Vero E6 cells in a 12-well plate at a density of 3.3 × 10^5 cells per well in complete DMEM.
Incubate plates overnight in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Infect Vero E6 cells with serially diluted stock icSARS-CoV-2-mNG for 1 hour with intermittent shaking.
Add cellulose overlay to the infected cells.
Fix and stain the cells 62 hours post-infection (hpi).
Enumerate plaques formed at specific dilutions, excluding clearings caused by pipetting or tears.
Reconstitute an aliquot vial of stock virus at −80°C in a 37°C water bath for 2–5 minutes.
Transfer the tube to a BSC and pulse-vortex mix for 10 seconds.
Prepare 1:10 serial dilutions by transferring 50 μL of stock into 450 μL of serum-free DMEM up to six times (to 10−6).
Retrieve plates of Vero E6 cells from the 37°C, 7% CO2 humidified incubator and bring them into the BSC.
Aspirate medium from the wells.
Add 100 μL diluted virus stock in four replicate wells to each respective well of the 12-well plates.
Work with one plate at a time to avoid cells from drying out.
Close the plate lid when not actively adding medium/sample to prevent desiccation or contamination of cell monolayers.
Add diluted virus in the following order: most dilute (10−6) to least dilute stock (10−1).
Seal the plates using parafilm.
Rock the plates gently by hand every 10 minutes for one hour.
Transfer the sealed plates from the BSC to a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Prepare the cellulose overlay medium while the plates are in the incubator.
Keep the cellulose overlay mixture in the 37°C water bath until ready for use.
After the incubation period, transfer the sealed plates from the incubator into the BSC.
Remove parafilm from the plates.
Add 1 mL of cellulose overlay mixture to each well containing the viral dilution.
Re-seal the plates with parafilm.
Transfer the resealed plates back to the 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Tilt the plates forward and back, side to side, to evenly distribute the overlay.
Incubate the plates for 62–66 hours.
Do not touch the plates during the entire incubation period.
Transfer the sealed plates from the incubator into the biological safety cabinet (BSC).
Remove the parafilm from the plates.
Shake the plates to agitate the cellulose overlay.
Discard the overlay according to CL3 biosafety protocol.
Wash the cells with 1 mL PBS to remove residual cellulose.
Pipette to remove the PBS carefully.
Add 1 mL fixative solution (4% formaldehyde) to the cells.
Incubate for 60 minutes at room temperature.
Remove formaldehyde from cells in the BSC with thimble connection.
Wash cells with 1 mL dH2O.
Add 0.5 mL staining solution to each well.
Incubate at room temperature for 10 minutes.
Remove staining solution and wash wells three times with 0.5 mL dH2O.
Examine the stained plates for plaques to determine stock titer.
Count the number of plaques in a minimum of two different viral dilutions.
Calculate the titer from each well.
Determine the average of two calculated titers to achieve accurate determination of your stock titer.
Prepare one T-25 flask coated with 2 mL Matrigel on the day of iPSC plating for differentiation.
Passage iPSC at 70%–80% confluence from a well of 6-well plate to the Matrigel-coated T25 flask with a seeding density of 50,000 cells per cm² in 3 mL mTeSR1 medium.
Gently agitate the flask to disperse colonies evenly.
Incubate overnight at 37°C in a 5% CO₂ humidified incubator.
Aspirate the mTeSR1 medium.
Add 4 mL of APEL2 medium containing 8 μM CHIR.
Replace the medium with fresh APEL2 containing 8 μM CHIR after 2 days.
After 92 h of CHIR treatment, replace the medium with 8 mL of fresh APEL2 medium supplemented with FGF-9 (200 ng/mL) and heparin (1 μg/mL).
Replace the medium with fresh APEL2 medium supplemented with FGF-9 and heparin every 2 days until day 7 of differentiation.
Prepare Trypsin-EDTA (0.05%), neutralization medium, and APEL2 medium pre-warmed to room temperature on day 7.
Aspirate the medium and wash the cells with 3 mL PBS.
Add 1 mL Trypsin-EDTA and incubate for 2 min in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Tap the flask to detach the cells after 2 min of trypsin incubation.
Monitor the cells under the microscope to ensure most cells have been detached.
Add 5 mL neutralization medium to the flask to neutralize trypsin.
Gently pipette the cells 6–8 times into single cell suspension using a 10 mL serological pipette.
Transfer the cells in suspension to a 15 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge at 400 × g for 3 min at room temperature.
Aspirate the supernatant and resuspend the cells in 3 mL APEL2 medium.
Remove 20 μL of cell suspension and perform cell counting using a Scepter 2.0 Cell counter or a hemocytometer.
Calculate and transfer the volume required to obtain 500K or 250K cells into 1.5 mL sterile centrifuge tubes.
Centrifuge the tubes at 400 × g for 2 min at room temperature to pellet the cells.
Prepare wide bore P200 tips by manually cutting off the end of tips with a sterile razor blade.
Collect the pellet using a P200 wide bore tip and transfer up to 4 pellets (500K or 250K cells per pellet) onto a six-well transwell.
Add 1.3 mL APEL2 medium containing 5 μM CHIR to the lower compartment of the transwell insert.
Place the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2, humidified incubator for 1 h.
Remove the medium and add 1.3 mL fresh APEL2 medium supplemented with FGF-9 and heparin.
Culture the pellets for 6 days in a 37°C, 5% CO2, humidified incubator.
Refresh APEL2 medium supplemented with FGF-9 and heparin every 2 days for 6 days.
Switch the culture medium to APEL2 medium without growth factors after 6 days of FGF-9 and heparin supplementation.
Refresh the APEL2 medium without growth factors every 2 days until the day of experiment (day 28).
Prepare a sterile fine forceps.
Place a razor blade and 10 cm culture plates on the bench.
Hold the upper plastic region of the transwell insert with one forceps.
Start cutting the transwell membrane along the edge from the bottom side, leaving approximately 2 mm attached to the insert.
Place the transwell insert on the sterile surface of a 10 cm culture plate.
Press the membrane with one forceps while gently pulling the transwell insert in the opposite direction to detach it.
Cut membranes around each organoid into approximately 1 cm × 1 cm squares using forceps and razor blade.
Supplement small volume (∼300 μL) of APEL medium underneath the membrane to prevent drying out.
Transfer each organoid with sterile forceps to a 24-well plate pre-filled with 1 mL APEL2 medium.
Place the plate in a 37°C, 5% CO2, humidified incubator.
Remove an aliquot of stock icSARS-CoV-2-mNeonGreen from −80°C storage.
Thaw virus in a 37°C water bath for 2–5 minutes.
Transfer the tube to the BSC and mix by pulse-vortexing for 10 seconds.
Dilute the stock virus to achieve working stocks of 10^3 PFU/500 μL and 10^5 PFU/500 μL in serum-free, drug-free advanced RPMI medium.
Remove medium from the kidney organoids.
Add 500 μL of either 103 or 105 PFU virus inocula directly into the wells.
Seal the plates using parafilm.
Incubate the organoids in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator for 1 hour.
Wash the organoids in 0.5 mL PBS three times to remove unbound virus.
Replenish with 0.5 mL fresh medium and incubate in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Collect supernatant from each well after 1.5 days post infection (dpi).
Centrifuge the collected supernatant at 500 × g for 10 minutes to remove cellular debris and particulates.
Transfer the supernatant to a new centrifuge tube.
Pulse-vortex to mix, then aliquot into externally threaded cryogenic tubes.
Store aliquots at −80°C for TCID50 assay.
Remove the medium and wash the organoids once with 0.5 mL PBS after 1.5 days (3 dpi).
Fix the organoids in 1 mL 4% PFA for 1 hour at room temperature.
Remove 4% PFA and wash the organoids in 0.5 mL PBS three times.
Keep the organoids in PBS at 4°C until further experiment is performed.
Seed Vero E6 cells in a 96-well plate at a density of 3 × 10^4 cells per well in complete DMEM.
Incubate the plates overnight in a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Remove virus-containing supernatant from kidney organoid cultures or retrieve from −80°C storage.
Thaw supernatants in a 37°C water bath for 2–5 minutes.
Mix thawed vials by pulse-vortexing for 10 seconds within the BSC.
Prepare 1:10 serial dilutions up to seven times (to 10−7) using sterile 1.5 mL tubes.
Aspirate medium from Vero E6 cell plates and add 200 μL of serially diluted supernatant in duplicate to each respective well.
Add 200 μL low-serum DMEM to each control well.
Seal the plates with parafilm.
Transfer the plates from the BSC to a 37°C, 5% CO2 humidified incubator.
Incubate for 5 days.
Remove plates from the incubator when cytopathic effects (CPE) are observed, typically after 5 days post infection.
Score each well for presence or absence of CPE by visual inspection using an inverted phase-contrast microscope.
Record the number of wells per dilution that are CPE-positive.
Fix and stain the 96-well plate if a physical record is desired (optional).
Use 0.2 ml PBS, 0.2 ml fixative solution (4% formaldehyde), 0.2 ml dH2O, and 0.1 ml staining solution for volume adjustments when fixing and staining.
Ensure control wells are absent of CPE and fluorescence under GFP exposure to confirm absence of cross-contamination.
Repeat the assay if CPE or fluorescence is present in control wells indicating contamination.
Calculate TCID50/mL according to the Kärber method using recorded data.
Wash the PFA-fixed kidney organoids once with PBS.
Place an organoid face-down in each well of an 8 well glass bottom chamber containing 150 μL blocking buffer.
Block the organoids for 2–3 h at room temperature on a shaker at 400 rpm.
Incubate the organoids with primary antibodies (1:200) in 150 μL blocking buffer at 4°C overnight on a shaker.
Wash the organoids in 150 μL wash buffer for 15 min each and repeat three times.
Incubate the organoids with 150 μL secondary antibodies (1:250) and LTL-Cy5 (1:100) in wash buffer at room temperature for 2–3 h.
Wash the organoids in 150 μL PBS for 10 min each.
Repeat the washing step twice.
Remove PBS from the well containing uninfected kidney organoid.
Locate the organoid using an inverted confocal microscope equipped with a 20× objective lens.
Use the 633 nm laser to locate proximal tubules labeled with LTL-Cy5.
Determine minimum background signal generated from the organoid using an optimum 488 nm laser power.
Capture nuclei of the cells in the organoids with 405 nm laser if organoids are stained with Hoechst33342.
Take multiple images from different fields of view to ensure autofluorescence does not produce a false positive signal.
Switch to icSARS-CoV-2-mNG infected kidney organoids.
Locate proximal tubules using the 633 nm laser with settings used in step 93.
Use the same 488 nm laser power as in step 94 to capture mNeonGreen+ cells in proximal tubules.
Take at least 10 images from multiple fields of view per organoid.
Run ImageJ and open confocal images of uninfected or infected SARS-CoV-2-mNG organoids captured by 488 nm laser.
Determine the empirical threshold level for mNeonGreen signal intensity.
Apply the same setting to all images captured under the same condition.
Go to “Process” in ImageJ and select “Make Binary”.
Count total LTL+ cells per field of view.
Count LTL+ mNeonGreen+ cells per field of view.
